whyByCategory.FED_CENTRAL_BANK: Fed communication is the primary driver of front-end rate expectations, and NQ is the index most sensitive to them.
whyByCategory.INTEREST_RATES: Rate expectations feed straight into long-duration tech valuations — NQ moves before the cash bond does.
whyByCategory.INFLATION: Inflation prints reset the policy path, which is the single largest repricing event NQ sees in a normal month.
whyByCategory.EMPLOYMENT: Labour data moves the policy path and is one of the few releases that reliably gaps the open.
whyByCategory.ECONOMIC_DATA: Second-tier data. Matters when it confirms or contradicts the current growth narrative, not on its own.
whyByCategory.WAR_MILITARY: Military escalation drives correlated risk-off across indices, energy and the dollar at once — position size, not direction.
whyByCategory.GEOPOLITICS: Geopolitical risk widens overnight ranges and makes the London-to-NY handover less reliable than usual.
whyByCategory.TARIFFS: Tariff headlines hit index futures immediately and hit semis hardest, because that is where the supply chain is.
whyByCategory.TRADE_POLICY: Trade policy sets the medium-term tone for the same names that carry the Nasdaq.
whyByCategory.US_POLITICS: Washington risk is mostly noise until it touches spending, the debt ceiling, or tariffs — then it is not.
whyByCategory.GLOBAL_POLITICS: Usually background. Matters when it changes a central bank's hand or a major trade relationship.
whyByCategory.FISCAL_POLICY: Fiscal news moves yields, and yields move NQ.
whyByCategory.SEMICONDUCTORS: Semis are the Nasdaq's engine — a large move here drags the index whatever the macro is doing.
whyByCategory.EARNINGS: Mega-cap earnings can move the index more than a Fed meeting, and the reaction is concentrated in one session.
whyByCategory.ENERGY: Energy feeds inflation expectations, which feed the policy path.
whyByCategory.CRYPTO: Correlates with Nasdaq as a risk proxy, and leads it at the extremes of positioning.
